October 1: Initial Architecture & Hardware Mapping!
Switched project focus to a differential-drive Line Follower Robot to build a complete 3D-printed hardware setup! Configured the core components on Amazon.eg to hit the exact $30 Tier 1 budget requirement.

I originally planned for a desktop controller, but pivoting to a autonomous robot makes the CAD housing and motor control integration much more engaging to document.

Here's how I structured the initial system layout:

Microcontroller: ESP32 DevKit V1 (30-pin) for processing sensor inputs and running PWM speed control for the motors.

Power Management: 2x 18650 Lithium-ion batteries in series (~7.4V output) connected directly to the L298N driver's power terminal.

Line Detection: 5-Channel IR Reflective Sensor module placed at the front underside of the chassis to read line deviation.

The primary engineering problem was figuring out how to supply clean power to the 3.3V ESP32 without risking overvoltage from the 7.4V battery pack:

The L298N motor driver module has an onboard 5V linear regulator.

By feeding the 7.4V battery pack into the L298N VCC and GND, I can pull regulated 5V output from the driver board directly into the ESP32 VIN / 5V pin.

The onboard ESP32 regulator then steps it down safely to 3.3V for logic operations and sensor power.

[7.4V Battery] ---> [L298N VCC] ---> [L298N 5V Out] ---> [ESP32 VIN]
The tl;dr is: Finalized the complete system schema, selected all required local components from Amazon.eg to lock the BOM at $30.00, and mapped out the initial power distribution topology for the upcoming chassis design.

Time spent this session: 1.0 hour
